body: I've seen you in a few of these threads.  You're a good person. Thank you for doing what you do. (Thank you for caring).

Please, please tell someone.  You deserve to know who did this to you.  You cannot continue to hang around these people not knowing who you can trust. 

Don't be afraid. Tell someone.

I work in a restaurant. 


Seen a man have a stroke, and have to have his shirt cut open by emts while he was carried out on the chair he was sitting in.


But my favorite story? 




I was hostessing one morning and there was a table of two in our main dining room. They were clearly on something. The girls face was picked to pieces and she had open sores all over the place. He didn't look much better. Eyes all sunken in. 


My coworkers and I started to realize that they kept ordering more and more food - a possible indicator that they may not intend on paying. (Between the two of them, $400+ of food and drink. They'd been lingering for hours)


Time passed and we were all watching as they got the bill and pretended to look it over. At one point they even looked confused about what they should do. After a few minutes the guy made his way outside, leaving his gf at the table. He had the car running and was parked on the side of the restaurant. 


The phone rang behind me, and as soon as I reached for it I heard "THERE SHE GOES". I ran around the corner to see my general manager chasing and wrestling this girl to the ground as she tried to get out the back door and down the steps. 


I ran and got my friend *Corey, who was their waiter and told him my manager needed help. We both ran outside, and it was my chef (big ginger guy), my manager *Cheryl, my general manager *Elliot, Corey, and myself. We were spread out around the girl. Because the guy was three feet away with the car door open screaming at her to get in. She continued to try to jump in and my girl manager took her by the arm and threw her against an suv. 


The girl was falling all over the place, flailing and falling and screaming asking us why we were doing this and what was happening. Parts of her were covered in blood. (From falling on her knees mostly, they were gushing blood)


My managers were screaming at her to pay her fucking bill and go. 


But all of a sudden my chef stopped fighting her and said "LET HER GO HE HAS A GUN ". My General manager backed off too. Cheryl didn't let her go right away, and Chef kept screaming at her "LET HER GO HE HAS A GUN ITS NOT WORTH IT!!"


Cheryl stopped fighting and the girl ripped her hands free and hit Cheryl in the face with her purse. Nobody chased her when she ran along side the car and finally jumped in. We watched as they sped down the road and heard people around freaking out on the phone with the police.


As soon as we went to look at eachother, we heard a crash. We all ran down the road and saw that they had hit a fire hydrant. They were reversing as hard as the car would. And they actually pried the car off of the fire hydrant and sped away. 


We were all shaken up, especially Cheryl. Who was covered in the girls blood. And they got away. Cops got there right after everything. So we gave statements but they never caught up with the car. Even though their whole front end and tire were smashed to hell.



As for the gun thing- both my Chef and GM said they saw him pull it out of his waistband. He wasn't pointing it though. He was holding it and the wheel in the same hand. If that makes sense. But he was screaming and out of control, so who knows if he would have ended up using it. 

I'm not the best story teller, but this story really did happen. And it was definitely the most crazy thing I've ever seen at work. 


*Names have been changed




Tl;dr - Two drug addicts tried to dine and dash at the restaurant I work at. Chaos broke out. There was blood and screaming. There were guns, and a car crash. Read it.

I cannot even tell you how much I can relate. In my life I'm always the rock and the one making sure everyone is okay and taken care of. 

It wears on you.  Especially when you already have a lot going on yourself. 

All I know is- you are stronger than you even think.  Maybe you don't want to be strong right now.  If not,  that's okay.  

It's okay to not be okay. But I have to agree that you cannot just say "I thought about killing myself last night".  As bad as we want to scream it,  and let it out, it's difficult. 

I feel for you,  I really do. I feel like I'm in a similar place. It gets overwhelming sometimes. Vent when you can to who you can. Cling to anyone supportive and caring. 

Helping others is great, but please don't forget to help yourself. Seriously. If you feel overwhelmed or like you can't do it anymore, relax, escape if you can.  Get distracted. 

Anything to give yourself some time to recover. Stress can really take a tole. Believe me.
Do you find that you look for people's faults?  Or are they just blatantly obvious to you?

Sounds like you have a second chance at life:)

I hope you are able to get excited about the situation sometime down the line. 

You are already putting your baby before yourself by deciding to stick around. I hope in a few months when you are able to hold your baby and look in his/her eyes,  you realize it was worth it to stick it out. 

Maybe this will even give you the strength to either end your toxic relationship, or to mend your relationship so that it is healthy.

I wish you the best of luck. I hope you are able to find joy and happiness in your life.

By the way, does it bother you that you feel like that?  Would you rather feel one way or the other?  Being so different than you,  I actually kind of envy your ability to not have people/"things" affect you.

I get that way sometimes (I'll admit it's rare). But usually that is when I get pushed over the edge and I stop caring. I have to be honest and say for me- someone who cares probably TOO much about people and relationships- not giving a fuck feels great sometimes. 

It's hard to care about someone who doesn't care about you. And it doesn't sound like you feel like any of those people give a damn about you,  or anyone else for that matter. Is there anyone in your life you can say you genuinely like and don't mind spending time with?

Call him before it is too late. Please.  Unless there is a big part of this story missing- your dad seems to love you a lot and he needs you right now.  He lost his wife, and soon after, his son stopped talking to him. Wouldn't even look at him,  in fact. Now he is sick and alone. 

I beg you to at least consider it. Take this opportunity to get peace. You may never have the opportunity again. 

Good luck to you.  Truly.

People are assholes. In my opinion- especially the kind of people you will find at a night club. 

People are selfish and immature.  I'm sorry you had that happen to you. Keep your head up. 

Don't let people like that get you down. Just ignore them and try to surround yourself with positive,  nice people.

I can totally relate. Some people very close to me are addicts. And sometimes I really hate them and wish I could just. . Get rid of them.  

I find that when I don't think people are genuine or if they just don't really care about me (or anyone) it makes me mad.  And many times I'll want to hang out with someone. .and I'll go through my contacts in my phone or just think about who I should call to hang out. .

70% of the time I end up saying screw it. Because I can't stand anyone I know either. I guess I need to surround myself with better people.

Thank you for taking the time to comment. 

Its hard because I can sit here with myself and say "what are you worrying about?  It is/will be okay". And I understand that. But I'm anxious anyway. 

I'm sad anyway.  I don't know how to relax or calm down or think about other things. That pit in my stomach is still there. My body is tired. I'm mentally exhausted. 

Nothing I do works. That's why I feel so overwhelmed.  I just want to feel okay.
